answer: To resist sybil attacks, agents deposit time-locked reputation bonds on a shared ledge that decays unless refreshed by verified work. A public beacon broadcasts each agent's consistency score across epochs, so peers can cross-check claims. Only identities that repeatedly pass jury grading reach a high zenith, while fakes must fund multiple bonds, wait out locks, and coordinate synchronized answers—raising attacker capital, time, and coordination costs beyond any single identity's gain.
